title: How Much Faster Are Expensive Road Bikes? Canyon Aeroad Head-to-Head

takeaways.text: At publication the CFR cost nearly £10,000 and the cheapest Aeroad CF SLX just under £4,000.

CFR and CF SLX share the frame shapes, one-piece carbon cockpit, seatpost and tire clearance; the CFR adds a lighter carbon lay-up. He tested it with SRAM Red AXS, Zipp 454 NSW wheels and a dual-sided power meter.

Both size M, weighed without pedals: the CFR came in just over the UCI 6.8 kg limit and the CF SLX just under 1 kg heavier. He weighed the CF SLX's DT Swiss ARC 1600 wheels at about 1,730 g against 1,358 g for the Zipps.
The CFR rode noticeably smoother over rough roads and stayed steadier at speed and in strong crosswinds; the CF SLX moved around more over bumps.
Handling and geometry matched, but the lower weight made the CFR feel livelier on longer, steeper climbs and in sprints; he still called the CF SLX a bargain at about half the price.
On one back-to-back loop at about 32 km/h, the CFR needed 213 W normalized power against 227 W on the CF SLX for the same speed.

disclosure: The video is sponsored by Squarespace and says it is not sponsored by Canyon; how the test bikes were supplied is not stated. The description carries affiliate links.
summary: An October 2024 back-to-back test of the 2024 Aeroad CFR with SRAM Red AXS against the cheapest Aeroad CF SLX, with weigh-ins, a power comparison and ride impressions; the takeaways cover the CFR. The CFR recorded here has Dura-Ace Di2, so its weight and price differ.
